note: Two texts written to close a hole the contradiction census found: CF-D004 (is the Hist one mind or many trees?) and CF-D006 (why is the Rootward Tide failing?) were registered as disputed and had no book anywhere in the game holding a position on either. A dispute with no source is a note dressed as a dispute, which is precisely what RI-LOR06's `positions[].held_by` field exists to prevent. Neither text adjudicates and neither knows about the other. CF-D006 position A is a real aggravation with genuinely good evidence and it is not the cause; a player who acts on it does real good and fixes nothing, which the registry requires and which this text must not give away.

books.title: The Fingers and the Hand: What the Lilmoth Keepers Hold
books.author: Sesh-Weth, before she went to the Court, and she has not withdrawn it
books.unreliability: A minority position stated plainly by somebody who has been argued out of it twice and has gone back to it both times. It is also the only account here that admits what would falsify it.

contradicts.on: whether the Hist are one thing or many

books.text:
The Imperials count the trees. They go along a river and they say: there is one, there is another one, that is two, and by the end of the season they have a number and they write the number down and they think they have described something.

The keepers at Helstrom say the opposite and say it beautifully. One tree. These are its fingers. What you are looking at when you look at a bole is a hand come up through the floor, and the hand is under everything, and there has never been more than one.

I was taught the Helstrom teaching and I no longer hold it, and I want to set out why, and I want to set out first the thing that would put me back.

If a keeper anywhere in this province could take a message at one well and have it come out of another, I would be wrong. That is the whole test. It is not a subtle test and it has been tried, and it has been tried by people who wanted it to work, and I have tried it myself with Ashul-Tei at four days' distance and an agreed hour and a phrase neither of us had used before. Nothing came through. We tried it three times and on the third we agreed to stop, because we had both begun to want it enough to imagine it.

But here is what I cannot get round, and it is the reason I do not simply count trees like a surveyor.

The old wells agree. Not the messages — the manner. A keeper who has sat at the well at Thorn all her life and a keeper who has sat at the well at Helstrom all his life will describe the same three things in the same order when you ask them what the tree is like to sit with, and they will use words that are not the same words and that mean the same thing, and neither of them has ever been to the other's well. I have collected this at every well I have been able to sit at. Almost all of them agree. Two do not.

The two that do not are the two that are known about and not discussed.

So here is what I hold. There was one. I think the Helstrom teaching is a memory and not a doctrine, and that once there was a hand under everything and the boles were fingers of it, and that this is why most wells still feel the same to sit at after however long it has been.

And I think some of the fingers have stopped listening.

Not died. A dead bole is a dead bole and you can see one and there are plenty. Stopped. The tree is standing, the sap runs, a hatchling that drinks there comes up looking at you the way they do — and the keeper at that well will tell you, if you have sat with her long enough that she will say it, that it is like sitting with a friend who has turned her face away and has not turned it back and is not going to.

The Helstrom keepers say this cannot happen because there is only one and one cannot be partly anything. The Imperials say this is nonsense because there are many and a tree that has gone quiet is simply a tree that was never anything. Both of them have an answer that costs them nothing.

I have sat at one of the two. I will not say which and I will not say where, and the reason is not mystery, it is that people would go and look, and there is nothing to see, and what a keeper who is sitting with a turned-away face does not need is company.

What I will say is that whatever else is true, this is not a question about how many trees there are. It is a question about how many of them are still answering, and no one is counting that, and I have thought for years that someone should be.

books.title: The Gem and the Root: A Statement of the Deep-Kin, for Anyone Who Will Take It
books.author: Teel-Ashaan, for the Xul-Aneekh, and it has been carried to four settlements
books.unreliability: Correct about a real crime, correct about its growth, and wrong that it is the cause. The evidence is genuinely good and it does not reach as far as the conclusion, and nothing in the world says so.

contradicts.on: why the wells are giving less back

books.text:
This is a statement and not an argument, because we have made the argument at Helstrom, at Thorn, at the hollow and at the Court, and each time we were thanked.

What happens when a thing dies in this country. It goes down. Not as a saying — as plumbing, and the polers know it and the keepers know it and the Court has four hundred years of it written in a book they will not open for a reader.

What happens when a thing dies in this country with a gem on it. It does not go down. It goes into the gem, and the gem goes on a cart, and the cart goes to Archon, and the gem goes on a ship.

That is root-theft. That is the whole of it and it requires no belief about trees at all.

Now the numbers, which we have and which have never once been asked of us.

The bond house at Archon enters soul gems out under three headings and we have had all three counted for nine years by people who work the crane. Nine years ago the three headings came to something under four hundred a season. This season the same three headings came to two thousand one hundred, and that is only what is entered, and the crane crews will tell you what goes out at night in a chest that is sealed and not opened per the standing arrangement.

Five times in nine years. On one wharf. In a province that the Empire says is quiet.

And in the same nine years every well from the Ladder to Thorn has given back less, and gone on giving back less, and the keepers who say so are the ones who have sat with them for forty years and know what a full return looks like because they have measured one.

We are told this is a coincidence. We are told it politely. The Wet Ledger's own survey — commissioned by them, paid for by them, and it is worth reading for the parts they did not think to leave out — says the cutting is what has done it, that thirty years of open wounds is more than any tree can carry, and we agree that the cutting is a wound and we have said so to the Ixtu-Vakh with knives in our hands.

But the cutting is above and the theft is a removal. A cut well is a tree bleeding into its own country. A gem on a ship is the country's blood in a foreign hold at Ebonheart, and there is no argument about which of those the ground gets back.

We are asked what we want. Here is what we want, and it is not the marsh and it is not the Empire out.

Stop the gems at Archon. Not the trade — the export. Let them be sold, let them be filled, let them be used here, and let anything that was taken out of this ground stay in this ground, and we will never raise the matter again.

We are told this is not possible. We are told it by people who have never once been unable to do a thing they wanted.

The last thing, and it is for our own people and not for the Empire. There are those among us who have begun to say that if the Court will not act and the Office will not act then we should stop the carts ourselves, and I have heard the word road said in a way I did not like. I am the one who wrote this. I have argued against it four times and I have won four times and I am not certain I will win a fifth, and I would rather the reader knew that we are running out of arguments than found out some other way.
